newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah edges up in dull late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah edges up in dull late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah edged up against the dollar in dull late trading on Tuesday on the back of sustained bullish sentiment, dealers said.
One local bank dealer said Singapore operators were forced to unload dollars they bought earlier because of fresh selling from Hong Kong and London operators.
"They might have to cut losses as fund managers needed the rupiah to pay for stock purchases," the dealer said.
Dealers said there were some customer orders to sell dollars following a rebound of the Jakarta stock market, which was later carried forward by London operators.
Spot rupiah edged up to 2,321.00/21.50 at 0850 GMT from an opening of 2,322.5/23.0.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,320.65/21.00 and 2,320.50/20.75, respectively.

"Sentiment on the rupiah remains bullish. There are still some selling pressures in the market for dollars, but I think the U.S. currency might be well supported at the 2,320.0 level," the local bank dealer said.
Dealers said operators were reluctant to sell dollars aggressiveley at the present level because it now was trading at the lower end of the central bank's floor rate.
One said the dollar-rupiah rate was expected to range between 2,320.0 and 2,323.0 on Wednesday.
The local bank dealer said swap rates were relatively stable in the afternoon after edging up earlier on the back of some uptrend in the interbank money market.
"People were still worried about last Friday's condition. They kept a close watch on the overnight rate," he said.
The dealer said liquidity was sufficient late in the afternoon, with overnight money trading at around 14.0 percent.
Overnight swap was at 0.5/0.6 and tom/next at 0.50/0.58.
The dealer said tom/next rate was relatively expensive, reflecting some underlying concern over the liquidity outlook.
One-month swap was quoted 15.25/16.00, two at 30.25/31.25, three at 47.25/47.75 and six at 96.50/97.50 points.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention rate at 2,310/2,502 and the conversion rate at 2,310/2,358 on Tuesday.
